text:
Noah Ostlund has gone from a part-time forward to one of Buffalo's busiest. At 22 he is playing 18:41 a night, up from 13:58 last season, and he is on the ice for 69% of the Sabres' power-play chances, up from 15%. A Buffalo News headline put it this way: "He's just a tool that you can use, anywhere."

The scoring has followed, if not all the way: 11 points in 20 games. His own chances are up to 0.91 expected goals per 60 from 0.45, and expected goals measure the quality of a player's looks. The goals have lagged, 4 on 5.65 expected, and Buffalo has scored 7.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, so our numbers have him due.

Forwards picked 11th to 21st since 2005 scored a median 0.31 points a game in their first full season. He is at 0.55. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows how he plays: he carries the puck in more than half the time, 67% of his shots come off the rush, and 20% of his setups cross the royal road. Evolving-Hockey had his value last season coming mostly from defense.
headline: Ostlund's breakout is built on minutes
